html: The oxidase that makes superoxide in a phagocyte is not a protein but an assembly, and that is what makes it a switch. Two of its subunits, CYBB and CYBA, sit in the membrane as the flavocytochrome b558, each destabilised without the other; CYBB alone carries the whole redox chain, a flavin and two hemes, with the binding site for NADPH on its cytosolic tail. The other components wait in the cytosol as a complex of one copy each of NCF1, NCF2 and NCF4, with NCF2 bridging the other two, while the small GTPase Rac is held apart and arrives loaded with GTP. Nothing happens until NCF1 is phosphorylated: in the resting protein a stretch between residues 286 and 340 folds back over its own tandem SH3 domains, and phosphorylation of Ser303, Ser304 and Ser328, by protein kinase C and by several other kinases, releases that clasp so the domains can reach the tail of CYBA. The cytosolic components then translocate as a unit, Rac binds the first repeats of NCF2, and the enzyme is complete. It works vectorially: electrons leave NADPH on the cytosolic face, pass to the flavin, cross the membrane through the two hemes and reduce oxygen on the far side, so the superoxide appears in the phagosome and not in the cytosol that made the fuel. The division of labour inside the assembly is sharp. NCF2 drives the first and rate-limiting step, from NADPH to the flavin, and must engage Rac for the later transfers; NCF1 only raises the affinity of the others, which is why it can be left out of a reconstituted system at high concentration yet is indispensable in a cell; NCF4 contributes targeting rather than catalysis, binding the phosphoinositide of the phagosomal membrane, so its loss removes the burst inside the phagosome while leaving the one released outside intact. Loss of any of the other four abolishes superoxide altogether, which is chronic granulomatous disease. For an exposure map the interesting point is that this switch can be thrown without any chemistry from the particle itself: inhaled particles that are chemically inert, carrying no metals, quinones or endotoxin, still raise the phosphorylated form of NCF1 and the oxidase subunits in exposed tissue. Expression and assembly are therefore two different statements about the same enzyme, and only the second of them is activation.
